description: Computation of directional optical flow in the Drosophila optic lobe. Direction-selective T4 neurons respond to moving bright edges (ON pathway), while T5 neurons respond to moving dark edges (OFF pathway). Four anatomical subtypes (a, b, c, d) code for front-to-back, back-to-front, upward, and downward motion.
coverage_notes: T4 and T5 cells are abundantly represented in the MaleCNS optic lobe dataset (>13,000 reconstructed neurons across both eyes).
limitations: Cell-type classification does not directly specify individual retinotopic receptive field coordinates or orientation tuning without optical column cross-referencing.

description: The biological implementation of the Hassenstein-Reichardt correlator in the Drosophila medulla. Medulla intrinsic Mi1 and transmedullary Tm3 neurons provide temporal delay differences and spatial separation required for direction-selective excitation onto T4 dendrites in the lobula plate.
coverage_notes: Extensively traced throughout the MaleCNS medulla (>9,000 reconstructed neurons across Mi1 and Tm3).
limitations: Biophysical delay mechanisms involve active conductances and graded potentials that are not directly represented by anatomical synapse counts.

display_name: Giant Fiber Escape & Flight Initiation (DNp01 → TTMn)
description: Rapid escape reflex circuit coordinating jump muscle contraction and flight wing depression. Bilateral descending neurons DNp01 (Giant Fibers) descend from the central brain into the ventral nerve cord (VNC), making strong monosynaptic connections with tergotrochanteral motor neurons (TTMn) and peripherally synapsing interneurons.
coverage_notes: Both bilateral DNp01 neurons (10001, 10002) and their VNC targets (e.g. 800146, 800178) are verified and traced in MaleCNS v1.0.
limitations: Electrical gap junctions present at the DNp01-TTMn synapse are invisible in EM chemical synapse weight tallies.

description: Sensory visual projection pathway transmitting looming collision signals from the lobula to premotor descending centers. Lobula Columnar 4 (LC4) neurons detect rapidly expanding dark edges and project to the posterior slope and gnathal ganglion to activate escape circuits.
coverage_notes: Around 300 LC4 projection neurons are cataloged in MaleCNS v1.0 across both hemispheres.
limitations: Downstream convergence of LC4 onto non-giant descending neurons involves multiple polysynaptic paths currently being mapped.

description: Glomerular sensory processing of airborne volatile odorants and pheromones in the antennal lobe. Uniglomerular projection neurons (PNs) receive sensory receptor inputs and project to the mushroom body calyx (for learned odor association) and the lateral horn (for innate behavioral responses).
coverage_notes: Projection neurons are represented by glomerulus-specific designations (e.g. DA1_lPN), but peripheral antennal receptor axons are severed at the nerve boundary.
limitations: Odor receptor identity cannot be deduced solely from structural connections without receptor-to-glomerulus mapping literature.

description: Spectral processing circuit comparing ultraviolet and green light. Distal medulla neurons Dm8 and Dm9 receive inputs from inner photoreceptors R7 (UV-sensitive) and R8 (blue/green-sensitive) in the medulla to mediate color preference and spectral discrimination.
coverage_notes: Dm8 and Dm9 interneurons exist in the annotations, but photoreceptor terminals (R7/R8) are largely omitted from the traced-only connection weights subset.
limitations: Photoreceptor input layer is largely truncated in the traced-only subset; spectral opponent comparisons cannot be fully reconstructed.

description: Mechanosensory acoustic vibration circuit in the antennal mechanosensory and motor center (AMMC) processing female-directed wing-vibration courtship song pulse trains.
coverage_notes: Specific AMMC acoustic interneuron subtypes (e.g., AMMC_B1) are not systematically mapped or annotated in the current MaleCNS v1.0 release.
limitations: Currently unsupported by verified annotation mappings in MaleCNS v1.0. Requires upcoming community annotation releases.
